scorecards.inningsCommentary: West Indies commenced their first innings at Sabina Park, aiming to set an imposing baseline total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 110 from KC Brathwaite, complemented by a commanding 109-run stand between SO Hetmyer and KC Brathwaite that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.16 RPO. Bangladesh's bowling response was spearheaded by Mehidy Miraz (5/93), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Concluding at 354/10 (111.6 ov), West Indies posted a competitive total, ensuring a closely matched contest.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: Bangladesh began their reply under scoreboard pressure, tasked with responding to West Indies's opening innings total. Tamim Iqbal anchored the innings with a resolute 47, providing backbone against a probing bowling attack while middle-order partnerships consolidated the position. West Indies's bowling response was spearheaded by JO Holder (5/43), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Reaching 149/10 (46.1 ov), Bangladesh's innings completed the first-innings exchange (205 Runs (West Indies)), shaping the strategic contours for the second half of the Test.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Sabina Park commenced with high tactical intensity as West Indies posted 354/10 (111.6 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Bangladesh countered with 149/10 (46.1 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: Shakib Hasan (6/33), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, JO Holder delivered a masterclass for West Indies (34 Runs & 11 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (West Indies 57%) and allowing West Indies to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Bangladesh faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. West Indies's bowling unit, bolstered by Shakib Hasan (86 Runs & 6 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing West Indies won by 166 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: West Indies's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Bangladesh produced fighting phases, West Indies won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
